title: The Stone Where Rain Stopped Falling

features.name: rain-pillar-calcifying
features.desc-on-touch: Rain falling through the shaft hardens as it falls—each drop adds a hair-thin layer of stone. You're watching millennia condense into minutes.

features.name: layered-stone-of-rainfall-years
features.desc-on-touch: Each band in the stone marks a year of rain, or a decade, or a century—you can't tell. The stone is reading its own memory of water.

features.name: the-wading-place
features.desc-on-touch: Rain on skin and stone both, the two of you counting the drops as if they could add up to something. Later she said the stone was just remembering how to be rain, and the rain was remembering how to be time.

features.name: drip-becoming-fossil
features.desc-on-touch: A single drop caught mid-fall, suspended in amber. It's been falling for so long that fall and stone have become synonymous.

features.name: water-clock-reading-geological-time
features.desc-on-touch: Each chamber fills and empties, but the emptying takes centuries. The clock still works, but patience became its only hand.

inscription: sediment is what remains when rain learns to stay

file.name: Rainfall_Record_NSW_1000_Years_Stratified.mp3
file.note: The archive recorded a century of rainfall compressed into audible time. At the end the drops sound like stone singing to itself.

reverie.title: REVERIE — rain becoming stone
narr: water on skin, water on stone, and she's saying the ground
is just learning a new language for falling. each drop adds
to the wall of the thing becoming. you stand in the creek
and watch the water choose to stay. later she said the whole
continent is just rain that finally learned how to remember.
the stone is the memory. the rain is still falling into it.

exits.label: down through the sediment layers, the weight returning
up where rain still falls freely
into the older stone, deeper striations
